## Natural history notes

A tiny acorn ant characterized by its small size, brown to yellowish-brown body, and compact, slow-moving workers that are often overlooked in leaf litter. In Florida, it is found in wooded habitats such as oak hammocks, pine-oak woods, forest edges, yards, and natural areas where fallen acorns, hollow twigs, and small plant cavities are available for nesting. Colonies are small and usually nest inside acorns, nuts, or dead twigs, while workers forage for tiny insects, scavenged material, nectar, and honeydew, making them part of the leaf-litter and canopy-edge food web.
